summary: Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku. He founded Ningen Zen.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at institutions including Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College under teachers including Enryo Inoue and Sarat Chandra Das. He was a professor at Toyo University (1916).
Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).
Elaine Fisher is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was a doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2010). She was appointed assistant professor at Stanford University in 2017.

Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned her PhD from the University of Warwick (~1991–1995). She became an emeritus professor at the University of Warwick (attested 1996).

Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University (~1963–1969) under Roger Brown, taught at Brown University (~1969–1971), and became a professor at UC Berkeley in 1971.

Elena Bashir is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Michigan (~1983–1988). She held appointments at the University of Chicago, serving on an editorial board (~2002–2020).
Elena Beccarini-Crescenzi was an Indologist who studied at the University of Florence until 1915 under Paolo Emilio Pavolini.

Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian history at Sapienza University of Rome (~1966–1971) under Luciano Petech. She became an associate professor at Sapienza University of Rome in 1980.
Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

Elena Mucciarelli is an Indologist who earned her PhD at the University of Tübingen (~2007–2010), later working there (2016–2017). She was a research fellow at Hebrew University (2017–2020) and became an assistant professor at the University of Groningen (2020).

Eli Franco (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who earned doctorates in Paris under Charles Malamoud and his Habilitation at Hamburg. He held the chair of Indology at the University of Leipzig (2004–2021).

Elijah George Halhed Impey (1818–1868) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Bombay Medical Service (1840), the Bombay Army (~1840–1865), and as Postmaster-General for the Bombay Presidency (1856–1868).

Elijah Sacvan Ary (born 1972) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (~2000–2007), where he completed his PhD under Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Elimar Benda (1890–1976) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who completed a Dr.iur. at the University of Jena (~1910–1913). He worked as a librarian at Berlin (1921–1922), Freiburg (1926–1936), and Heidelberg (1936–1940).

Elimar Max Grube (1851–1891) was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Rudolf von Roth, and Albrecht Weber, earning his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (1874–1875).

Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his PhD at Columbia University (1956–1960). He taught at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006).

Elisa Freschi (born 1977) is an Indologist and philosopher who completed her doctorate under Raffaele Torella (~2003–2007). She held posts at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Vienna (~2017–2023), and the University of Toronto (~2021).
Elisa Ganser is an Indologist who worked as an SNF project collaborator at the University of Zurich (2018) and as a lecturer at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Elisabeth Kreyenborg (born 1897) was an Indologist who earned her PhD at the University of Münster under Richard Schmidt (~1925–1930). She served as a librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1943–1950).
